description: Arcs whose radii are the wrong way round, which d3 does not refuse: it swaps them, so an arc written inside-out draws exactly the ring an arc written the right way round would. The five here are the cases that separate swapping from rejecting — a normal ring, the same ring written inverted, an arc given only an inner radius (its outer radius defaults to zero, so swapping turns it into a solid wedge of that size), a negative outer radius, which collapses to a point at the centre, and a slice of no angle at all. Each still produces an item; the third is the one a specification is most likely to write by accident, and drawing nothing for it is the difference between a donut and an empty canvas. They are also turned by an `angle`, which every mark drawn through `markItemPath` takes and an arc is one of them — the wedge is rotated about its own centre, which for a shape d3 draws about the origin is the same as upstream's rotated bound context.
